items.title: Endoville Backend API Documentation
items.text: Welcome to the Endoville Backend API Documentation.

items.title: Overview
items.text: This API provides user management, authentication, account activation, and blog content.

items.title: Base URLs
items.text:
• Users: https://api.endovillehealth.com/api/users/
  • Blogs: https://api.endovillehealth.com/api/blogs/
  • Products: https://api.endovillehealth.com/api/products/
  • Orders: https://api.endovillehealth.com/api/orders/

items.title: Authentication
items.text: Most endpoints require JWT authentication. You'll receive access and refresh tokens after successful login.

items.title: API Endpoints
items.text:
• User Registration
  • Account Activation
  • OTP Management
  • Authentication
  • Google OAuth Login
  • User Profile
  • Staff Check
  • Blogs
  • Products
  • Orders
  • Payments
  • Shipments

items.title: Response Format
items.text: All responses are in JSON format.

items.title: Success Response
items.text:
{
  "message": "Operation successful",
  "data": { ... }
}

items.title: Error Response
items.text:
{
  "field_name": ["Error message"],
  "non_field_errors": ["General error message"]
}

items.title: Status Codes
items.text:
• 200 OK - Request successful
  • 201 Created - Resource created successfully
  • 400 Bad Request - Invalid request data
  • 401 Unauthorized - Authentication required
  • 404 Not Found - Resource not found
  • 500 Internal Server Error - Server error

items.title: Account Activation
items.text:
Activate a user account using the OTP received via email.

EndpointAuthenticationRequest BodyFields 
POST /api/users/activate/

No authentication required.

{
  "email": "user@example.com",
  "otp": "123456"
}
Field Type Required Description email string Yes User's email address otp string Yes 6-digit OTP code received via email

items.title: Response
Error Cases
items.text:
• Invalid OTP: The OTP code is incorrect
  • Expired OTP: The OTP has expired (valid for 5 minutes)
  • Already Activated: The account is already active
  • User Not Found: No user exists with the provided email

items.title: Notes
items.text:
• OTPs expire after 5 minutes
  • OTPs can only be used once
  • After activation, the user can log in
  • If the OTP expires, use the resend OTP endpoint to get a new one

items.title: Example Request
items.text:
curl -X POST https://api.endovillehealth.com/api/users/activate/ \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "email": "user@example.com",
    "otp": "123456"
  }'

items.title: Comments
Notes
items.text:
• Unauthenticated users can only read posts and comments.
  • Non-staff authenticated users can create comments; they may delete only their own comments.
  • Only staff can create/update/delete authors and posts, and only staff can edit comments.

items.title: Categories & Subcategories
items.text:
Blogs support categories and subcategories. Categories list and retrieve responses include nested subcategories.

GET /api/blogs/categories/{id}/

Returns the same structure as list items: category fields plus a subcategories array.

GET /api/blogs/subcategories/
GET /api/blogs/subcategories/{id}/

Subcategories have their own endpoints. Each includes category (ID) and category_name.

  • Categories: Staff CRUD at /api/blogs/categories/{id}/ for create, update, delete.
  • Subcategories: Staff CRUD at /api/blogs/subcategories/{id}/ for create, update, delete.
  • A post can belong to multiple subcategories using the subcategories field on the post endpoints.

items.title: Related Products
items.text:
Posts support a many-to-many relationship with products:

  • related_products (writable): Array of product IDs. Use when creating or updating a post.
  • related_products_details (read-only): Array of lightweight product objects {id, name, slug, price, image_urls} for display.

items.title: Google OAuth Login
items.text:
Login or sign up using Google OAuth.

EndpointAuthenticationRequest BodyFields 
POST /api/users/google-login/

No authentication required (to get tokens).

{
  "access_token": "ya29.a0AfH6SMC..."
}
Field Type Required Description access_token string Yes Google OAuth access token

items.title: Response
Error Cases
items.text:
• Missing Token: access_token field is required
  • Invalid Token: Google access token is invalid or expired
  • No Email: Google account doesn't have an email address
  • API Error: Error communicating with Google API

items.title: How It Works
items.text:
1. Client obtains Google OAuth access token from Google
  2. Client sends the access token to this endpoint
  3. Server verifies the token with Google API
  4. Server creates or links the user account
  5. Server returns JWT tokens for authentication

items.title: Frontend (JavaScript)
items.text:
// Using Google Sign-In SDK
google.accounts.oauth2.initTokenClient({
  client_id: 'YOUR_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID',
  scope: 'email profile',
  callback: (response) => {
    const accessToken = response.access_token;
    // Send accessToken to /api/users/google-login/
  }
}).requestAccessToken();

items.title: OAuth Playground (Testing)
items.text:
1. Go to Google OAuth Playground
  2. Select "Google OAuth2 API v2" → "userinfo.email" and "userinfo.profile"
  3. Authorize and exchange for tokens
  4. Use the access token in your API request

items.title: Notes
items.text:
• If the user doesn't exist, a new account will be created automatically
  • The account is automatically activated (is_active=True)
  • If a user with the same email exists, the Google account will be linked
  • The user's profile image (image_url) is set from Google's profile picture on sign-up and updated on each Google sign-in
  • JWT tokens work the same as regular email/password login
  • The Google access token is only used for verification, not stored

items.title: Example Request
items.text:
curl -X POST https://api.endovillehealth.com/api/users/google-login/ \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "access_token": "ya29.a0AfH6SMC..."
  }'

items.title: Staff Check
items.text:
Check whether the currently authenticated user is a staff user.

EndpointAuthentication 
GET /api/users/is-staff/

JWT required.

items.title: Response
Authentication
items.text:
Login with email, password, and OTP to receive JWT tokens.

EndpointAuthenticationRequest BodyFields 
POST /api/users/login/

No authentication required (to get tokens).

{
  "email": "user@example.com",
  "password": "securepassword123",
  "otp": "123456"
}
Field Type Required Description email string Yes User's email address password string Yes User's password otp string Yes 6-digit OTP code for additional security

items.title: Response
Error Cases
items.text:
• Invalid Credentials: Email or password is incorrect
  • Inactive Account: Account is not activated
  • Invalid OTP: OTP code is incorrect or expired
  • Expired OTP: OTP has expired (valid for 5 minutes)
  • Used OTP: OTP has already been used

items.title: Access Token
items.text:
• Lifetime: 3 hours
  • Usage: Include in Authorization header for authenticated requests
  • Format: Bearer <access_token>

items.title: Refresh Token
items.text:
• Lifetime: 7 days
  • Usage: Use to get a new access token when it expires
  • Endpoint: /api/token/refresh/ (if implemented)

items.title: Using the Access Token
items.text:
Include the access token in the Authorization header:

curl -X GET https://api.endovillehealth.com/api/users/profile/ \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer eyJ0eXAiOiJKV1QiLCJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9..."

items.title: Notes
items.text:
• Both email/password and OTP must be valid
  • The account must be activated (is_active=True)
  • OTP is single-use and expires after 5 minutes
  • Maximum of 3 OTP verification attempts
  • The access token should be stored securely (e.g., in localStorage or secure cookies)
  • Use the refresh token to obtain a new access token before it expires

items.title: Example Request
items.text:
curl -X POST https://api.endovillehealth.com/api/users/login/ \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "email": "user@example.com",
    "password": "securepassword123",
    "otp": "123456"
  }'

items.title: OTP Management
items.text:
Resend OTP for account activation.

EndpointAuthenticationRequest BodyFields 
POST /api/users/send-otp/

No authentication required.

{
  "email": "user@example.com"
}
Field Type Required Description email string Yes User's email address

items.title: Response
Error Cases
items.text:
• User Not Found: No user exists with the provided email
  • Already Active: The account is already activated (no need for OTP)
  • Email Required: The email field is missing

items.title: Notes
items.text:
• Use this endpoint if you didn't receive the OTP or if it expired
  • A new OTP will be generated and sent to the email address
  • The previous OTP (if any) will be invalidated
  • The new OTP is valid for 5 minutes
  • Maximum of 3 attempts per OTP before it's locked

items.title: Example Request
items.text:
curl -X POST https://api.endovillehealth.com/api/users/send-otp/ \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "email": "user@example.com"
  }'

items.title: Payments
items.text: Create and track payments for orders.

items.title: Overview
items.text:
• User payments: create a payment for your own order and view payment status/links.
  • Staff payments: can view and manually update any payment.
  • Payment credentials: managed via staff API (no admin UI required).
  • Orders are considered fully paid when the sum of completed payments is >= the order total. If a completed payment is deleted (or changed), the flag is recalculated automatically.

items.title: Fully Paid Rules
items.text:
• Only payments with status="completed" and is_deleted=false count toward the order total.
  • If an order is already fully paid, creating a new payment will return an error (both user and staff endpoints).

items.title: Providers
items.text:
• intasend (link or STK push)
  • stripe (checkout)
  • cash (manual)
  • other (manual)

items.title: Base URLs
items.text:
• User payments: /api/orders/payments/
  • Staff credentials: /api/orders/payment-credentials/
  • Staff manage payments: /api/orders/staff/payments/

items.title: Authentication
items.text:
• All endpoints require authentication.
  • Staff endpoints additionally require is_staff=true.

items.title: Payment Credentials (Staff API)
items.text:
Payment provider credentials are global for the whole app (not per user) and are stored in orders.PaymentCredentials.

Create credentials (staff)List credentials (staff)Update credentials (staff) 
POST /api/orders/payment-credentials/

Request body:

{
  "provider": "intasend",
  "environment": "sandbox",
  "api_key": "YOUR_PUBLISHABLE_KEY",
  "private_key": "YOUR_SECRET_OR_PRIVATE_KEY",
  "is_active": true
}

Notes: - private_key is write-only (never returned). - Response includes has_private_key: true/false. - Only one credentials row can be active per (provider, environment).

GET /api/orders/payment-credentials/

PATCH /api/orders/payment-credentials/{id}/

Example rotate secret key:

{
  "private_key": "NEW_SECRET_KEY"
}

items.text:

items.title: Cost Price (Staff-only)
items.text:
Products and variants include a cost_price field, but it is only returned in API responses when the requester is a staff user.

  • Public/non-staff: cost_price is omitted from responses.
  • Staff: cost_price is included for both products and nested variants.

items.title: Currency conversion (non-staff)
items.text: For non-staff product and variant responses, prices include display_currency and currency_symbol. Prices use the primary currency (e.g. USD) by default. Use ?currency=CODE to convert. The API uses the Currency usd_rate for conversion when ?currency= is passed. - Default: When no ?currency= param is passed, the primary currency (typically USD) is used. Prices include display_currency and currency_symbol. - With ?currency=CODE: Prices are converted; response includes display_currency, currency_symbol, and converted price. - Staff: Always see stored prices; display_currency and currency_symbol are included (primary/USD).

items.title: Currencies
items.text:

    "password": "securepassword123"
  }'

items.title: Shipments
items.text: Track shipping progress for orders.

items.title: Base URLs
items.text:
• User shipments: /api/orders/shipments/
  • Staff shipments: /api/orders/staff/shipments/
  • Staff shipment events: /api/orders/staff/shipment-events/

items.title: Authentication
items.text:
• All endpoints require authentication.
  • Staff endpoints additionally require is_staff=true.

items.title: Shipping Status Steps
items.text:
• ORDER_PLACED
  • DISPATCHED
  • OUT_FOR_DELIVERY
  • DELIVERED

Users see a timeline via events[] on the shipment response.

items.title: User Endpoints
items.text:
ListRetrieve 
GET /api/orders/shipments/

Success (200):

[
  {
    "id": 55,
    "status": "ORDER_PLACED",
    "carrier": "",
    "tracking_number": "",
    "tracking_url": "",
    "estimated_delivery_at": null,
    "delivered_at": null,
    "created_at": "2026-01-19T10:00:00Z",
    "updated_at": "2026-01-19T10:00:00Z",
    "events": [
      {
        "id": 100,
        "status": "ORDER_PLACED",
        "message": "Order placed",
        "location": "",
        "occurred_at": "2026-01-19T10:00:00Z"
      }
    ]
  }
]

GET /api/orders/shipments/{id}/

items.title: Staff Endpoints
items.text:
Update shipment (staff)Add shipment event (staff) 
PATCH /api/orders/staff/shipments/{id}/

Request body:

{
  "status": "DISPATCHED",
  "carrier": "DHL",
  "tracking_number": "TRK-123",
  "tracking_url": "https://carrier.example.com/track/TRK-123",
  "estimated_delivery_at": "2026-01-25T10:00:00Z"
}

POST /api/orders/staff/shipment-events/

Request body:

{
  "shipment": 55,
  "status": "DISPATCHED",
  "message": "Dispatched from warehouse",
  "location": "Nairobi",
  "occurred_at": "2026-01-19T12:00:00Z"
}

Notes: - Staff should update Shipment.status and add a matching ShipmentEvent so users see the timeline update. - When the shipment is delivered, set status=DELIVERED and set delivered_at.

items.title: Getting Started
items.text: Quick start guide for using the Endoville Backend API.

items.title: Prerequisites
items.text:
• A valid email address
  • Internet connection
  • HTTP client (curl, Postman, or similar)

items.title: 1. Register
items.text:
Create a new account:

POST /api/users/register/

You'll receive an email with an OTP code.

items.title: 2. Activate Account
items.text:
Activate your account using the OTP:

POST /api/users/activate/

items.title: 3. Login
items.text:
Login with your credentials and OTP:

POST /api/users/login/

You'll receive JWT tokens (access and refresh).

items.title: 4. Use Access Token
items.text:
Include the access token in authenticated requests:

Authorization: Bearer <access_token>

items.title: Quick Example
items.text:
# 1. Register
curl -X POST https://api.endovillehealth.com/api/users/register/ \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "email": "user@example.com",
    "first_name": "John",
    "last_name": "Doe",
    "password": "securepassword123"
  }'

# 2. Check email for OTP (e.g., "123456")

# 3. Activate
curl -X POST https://api.endovillehealth.com/api/users/activate/ \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "email": "user@example.com",
    "otp": "123456"
  }'

# 4. Login
curl -X POST https://api.endovillehealth.com/api/users/login/ \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "email": "user@example.com",
    "password": "securepassword123",
    "otp": "654321"
  }'

# Response includes access token - use it for authenticated requests

items.title: Alternative: Google Login
items.text:
You can also login using Google OAuth:

POST /api/users/google-login/

No registration or activation needed - account is created automatically.
